title: pvVisItH5NimrodReader
body:
## pvVisItH5NimrodReader

Reads HDF5 output of NIMROD, the extended-MHD code for fusion plasmas, in its H5Nimrod data model (.h5nimrod): a curvilinear mesh with node- and cell-centred fields over several time steps. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native NIMROD reader. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The plugin rejects unstructured NIMROD meshes; only the structured (curvilinear) layout is read.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItH5NimrodReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItH5NimrodReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from NIMROD HDF5 data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The NIMROD HDF5 plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields stored in the file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single NIMROD HDF5 file to read (.h5nimrod); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The NIMROD HDF5 plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the NIMROD HDF5 meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The H5Nimrod plugin reports a curvilinear mesh; take the name from the reader's available list. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from NIMROD HDF5 data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The NIMROD HDF5 plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields stored in the file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItH5NimrodReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
